TimePeriod: Patriarchal era through the monarchy; the name still appears in the Gospels (Matthew 15:22)
Region: The land of Canaan, from Sidon to Gaza and inland to the Jordan (Genesis 10:19)
History: This entry covers the Canaanites as a people; the land and its city-states are covered by the Canaan entry in Civilizations. The Canaanites descend from Canaan, son of Ham (Genesis 10:15-19), whose sons give the coastal and inland peoples their names. The name is sometimes used broadly for all the pre-Israelite inhabitants: 'the Canaanite was then in the land' when Abram arrived (Genesis 12:6). Deuteronomy 7:1 counts the Canaanites among the seven nations Israel was to displace, and Joshua 3:10 names them among the peoples the living God would drive out. In Judges the pattern reverses: Israel 'dwelt among the Canaanites' and took their daughters in marriage (Judges 3:5), and the peoples and their gods became the standing test of the covenant.
Culture: City-dwellers and farmers of walled towns and open villages, trading along the coastal road and the Jordan Valley.
Religion: The gods of Canaan, Baal and Asherah and the gods of the city-states, whose worship Israel was warned against and repeatedly adopted.
BibleConnection: The Canaanites are the peoples of the Promised Land: the inhabitants Israel was told to displace, the neighbors Israel lived among, and the constant covenant test of Judges.
RelatedEvents: The Twelve Spies and Israel's Unbelief; The Walls of Jericho
